land.text: northern Khwarezm, held for the Jochid ulus

predecessors.note: The golden-horde dossier draws Khwarazm as Horde land and records the 1383 restoration of authority.

land.text: Khwarezm, after Timur razed Gurganj in 1388

successors.note: The timurid-empire dossier dates Khwarazm's entry to Cliopatria's 1402 shape (confidence 1). Kath and Khiva went to Timur earlier, in the peace after the 1373 campaign (ledger); the timurid-empire dossier has no event for that.

capitals.name: Urgench (Gurganj)
capitals.note: The Sufi page names Urgench, Kath and Khiva; the Tokhtamysh page names the capital as '(old) Gurganj', razed in 1388. Coordinates are Konye-Urgench (Kunya-Urgench), the old Gurganj.

rulers.name: Husain Sufi
rulers.note: Ruler list 'Husain (1361-1372)'; took Urgench and the northern part of Khwarezm; coins from 1364; 'died during the siege' of Urgench in 1372. The list opens with Aq Sufi (1359-1361), before this dossier's start.

rulers.name: Yusuf Sufi
rulers.note: List 'Yusuf (1372-1379)'; made the peace in which Timur received Kath and Khiva; 'died in the middle of the siege' of 1379.

rulers.name: Balankhi
rulers.note: List 'Balankhi (1380)'; the page mentions him nowhere else.

rulers.name: Maing
rulers.note: List 'Maing (1380)'; the page mentions him nowhere else.

rulers.name: Sulayman Sufi
rulers.note: List 'Sulayman (1380-1388)'; the text spells Suleiman, allied with Tokhtamysh and revolted in 1387. 1379-1380 is an interregnum of the list (the burned city).

correction.text: 'Urgench and the rest of the northern part of Khwarezm', with Kath and Khiva

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row (the Golden Horde shapes of the period cover Khwarazm). The page names Urgench, Kath and Khiva and gives no boundary or area; the gazetteer's Khwarezm region (213,000 km2) is the researcher's reading. Valid until the peace with Timur (c.1373), which took Kath and Khiva away.

correction.text: Khwarezm without Kath (Beruniy) and Khiva, which Timur received in the peace: Urgench and the rest of northern Khwarezm

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (repair 2026-10-19). 'Yusuf Sufi concluded a peace with Timur in which Timur received Kath and Khiva' (Sufi page; year not given, bridged to 1373). The two 60 km circles are the researcher's reading of 'southern Khwarezm'. After the 1379 siege the dynasty persisted as a Timurid and then Horde dependant (vassal events), so the shape is kept to 1388, when Timur razed Gurgānj.

ledger.note: c.1361: Husain Sufi holds Urgench. Infobox founding 'c. 1361'; Husain Sufi, a son of Naghday, 'took control of Urgench and the rest of the northern part of Khwarezm'; coins were minted for him from 1364. The Golden Horde's White Horde side loses Khwarazm.
1372: Timur's first campaign. The page lists Timur's campaigns of 1372, 1373, 1379 and 1387; in 1372 'Husain Sufi died during the siege' of Urgench and Yusuf Sufi succeeded.

c.1373: Yusuf Sufi cedes Kath and Khiva to Timur. 'Husain Sufi's refusal to return southern Khwarezm caused Timur to go to war against him in 1372'; 'This led Timur to undertake a second campaign against him in 1373'; Yusuf Sufi 'concluded a peace with Timur in which Timur received Kath and Khiva'. The page gives no year for the peace; it follows the second campaign and precedes the siege of 1379, and 1373 is the bridging year (the reviewer proposed 1372 or 1373 at confidence 3; the page does not date it, so it stays at 1). Kath is Beruniy (Beruniy page: 'Historically, Beruniy was known as Kath'; 41.68 N, 60.75 E), which the gazetteer lacks; Khiva is the place Khiwa. The page also says Husain Sufi had seized Kath and Khiva, 'which were allocated to the Chagatai khans', without a year.

1379: Timur takes Urgench. 'the subjugation of Khwarazm and Urgench in the Siege of Urgench (1379)' (Timur page); 'a general massacre followed and the city was burned' (Sufi page). The Sufi infobox gives this as the dissolution (1379); the dynasty carried on under Sulayman.

region.text: Urgench and the rest of northern Khwarezm

ledger.note: 1379: the Sufi dynasty becomes a Timurid dependant after the siege. 'the subjugation of Khwarazm and Urgench in the Siege of Urgench (1379)' (Timur page); the Sufi page has the city burned after Timur 'finally did capture it by force' and Yusuf Sufi dead 'in the middle of the siege', its infobox ends the dynasty in 1379, yet the ruler list continues with Balankhi, Maing and Sulayman from 1380, and the Sufids 'continued to rule Khwarezm intermittently as governors of the Timurid Empire'. The page does not call this a vassalage; that is the reading.

region.text: Urgench and the rest of northern Khwarezm

ledger.note: 1383: Timurid authority lapses. 'In 1383, taking advantage of Timur's preoccupation with affairs in Persia, Tokhtamysh restored the Golden Horde's authority over the semi-autonomous Ṣūfī Dynasty in Khwarazm' (Tokhtamysh page); the page does not say Timur's overlordship ended, that is the reading.

region.text: Urgench and the rest of northern Khwarezm, the 'semi-autonomous Ṣūfī Dynasty in Khwarazm'

ledger.note: 1383: the Sufi dynasty is again a Golden Horde dependant. Tokhtamysh 'restored the Golden Horde's authority over the semi-autonomous' Ṣūfī Dynasty in Khwarazm (Tokhtamysh page). Mirror of golden-horde /ledger/15 (counterpart there the string 'Sufi dynasty of Khwarazm'); replaces the rename placeholder of the first version.
1387: Sulayman revolts. He 'allied with the khan of the Golden Horde, Tokhtamysh, and in 1387 revolted'; Timur then 'overran Khwarezm and crushed the rebellion'.
1388: Timur razes Gurganj. Timur 'overthrew the Sufi Dynasty of Khwarazm for its collusion with Tokhtamysh' and 'razed to the ground its capital' in 1388.

region.text: Urgench and the rest of northern Khwarezm, the 'semi-autonomous Ṣūfī Dynasty in Khwarazm'

ledger.note: 1388: Timur overthrows the dynasty and the Horde loses its dependant. 'He overthrew the Ṣūfī Dynasty of Khwarazm for its collusion with Tokhtamysh and razed to the ground its capital, [(old) Gurgānj], in 1388' (Tokhtamysh page). Mirror of golden-horde /ledger/17.
1388: the Sufi dynasty is overthrown. The Sufi page's ruler list ends Sulayman's reign in 1388 and has the Sufids continue only as Timurid governors until the Shaybanids took Khwarezm in 1505.

wars.name: Timur’s campaigns against Khwarazm
wars.outcome: Campaigns in 1372, 1373, 1379 and 1387 (Sufi page) and 'five military campaigns' (Timur page, undated); Urgench fell in 1379 and Gurganj was razed in 1388, ending the dynasty.
wars.note: Khwarazm 'suffered the most' of Timur's conquests because it 'repeatedly rose against him' (Timur page).

certainty.note: Oasis frontiers along the lower Amu Darya; no line is recorded.

sources.title: Sufi dynasty
sources.note: Sufi dynasty of Khwarazm: infobox founding c.1361, dissolution 1379; Husain Sufi took Urgench and northern Khwarezm, coins from 1364; Timur's campaigns 1372, 1373, 1379, 1387; Yusuf 1372-1379; Sulayman revolted 1387 and the list ends 1388; Sufids Timurid governors to 1505. Re-read 2026-10-19: Kath and Khiva seized by Husain ('allocated to the Chagatai khans'); campaigns 1372, 1373; peace under Yusuf in which Timur received Kath and Khiva (no year); siege of 1379; ruler list Aq Sufi 1359-1361, Husain 1361-1372, Yusuf 1372-1379, Balankhi 1380, Maing 1380, Sulayman 1380-1388; infobox dissolution 1379.

sources.title: Timur
sources.note: Timur: five campaigns against Khwarazm (undated), the Siege of Urgench (1379).

sources.title: Tokhtamysh
sources.note: Tokhtamysh restored the Golden Horde's authority over the Sufi dynasty in 1383; Timur overthrew the dynasty and razed old Gurganj in 1388. Re-read 2026-10-19: 1383 restoration of Horde authority over the Sufi dynasty; 1388 overthrow.

sources.title: Beruniy
sources.note: Repair 2026-10-19: 'Historically, Beruniy was known as Kath'; 41.683 N, 60.750 E; nothing on the 14th century.

notes:
A short-lived Khwarazmian state between the Golden Horde and Timur, flagged by ia-02-b and ia-02-c (sufi-dynasty-of-khwarazm, 1383-1388 and 1402). The golden-horde dossier records its 1383-1388 tie to the Horde with the counterpart string 'Sufi dynasty of Khwarazm'; the timurid-empire dossier dates the Timurid hold on Khwarazm to 1402 at confidence 1.

Dates disagree: the Sufi infobox ends the dynasty in 1379 (Timur's siege), the ruler list and the Tokhtamysh page have it overthrown in 1388, and the Sufi page has the Sufids as Timurid governors until 1505; the page gives the founding as c.1361 but coins only from 1364. The 'five campaigns' of the Timur page are undated; the Sufi page dates four (1372, 1373, 1379, 1387). The 1372 and 1373 campaigns are not separate events because the pages do not say what changed hands. The status change of 1383 is a rename-type placeholder so that the Horde's tint (golden-horde dossier) has an anchor here.

Region name: Khwarezm exists in the gazetteer; Kath and Khiva are inside it. Edigu's occupation of Khwarazm (1405-1412) and Shah Rukh's expulsion are in the golden-horde and timurid dossiers.


[Repair ia-02-x, 2026-10-19] Reviewer findings applied after reopening the Sufi dynasty and Tokhtamysh pages: (1) loss of Kath and Khiva to the Timurid Empire dated 1373 at confidence 1 (the Sufi page gives the peace but no year; the reviewer's c3 would claim a date the page does not give), with the keyframe split at 1373; Kath is placed by the Beruniy page's coordinates (60.75 E, 41.68 N). (2) The rename placeholder of 1383 is replaced by vassal_start 1383 / vassal_end 1388 with golden-horde (the golden-horde dossier should use the slug sufi-dynasty-of-khwarazm instead of the string). (3) The 1379 siege: vassal_start 1379 / vassal_end 1383 with timurid-empire at c2, the 1379 'dissolution' of the infobox being read as the end of independence, not of the dynasty (the ruler list continues to 1388); the timurid-empire dossier has no matching event and dates Khwarazm's entry to 1402 at c1. (4) Rulers follow the page's list (Balankhi 1380, Maing 1380, Sulayman 1380-1388). Counterpart direction of the vassal events follows the reviewer (the vassal's dossier names the suzerain; the schema says the counterpart is the vassal).
